overall: MARGINAL overall: calm on the Coron side and in the south, breezy in the west with a midday lull, Nangalao still POOR
limiterDetail: The main limiter is wind in the west: 16 kt now at Nangalao (gusts 21, staying 13–18 kt all day and night), 14 kt at Ciron (13–17 kt all day), 13 kt at Cabunlawan and Decabaitot and 10.5 kt at Barangonan (all building to 14–17 kt about 7–9 AM, easing to 9–10 kt about 1–4 PM, then 15–16 kt again from about 8 PM). Linapacan holds 8–12 kt and Alava and Binudac 7–12.6 kt. The Coron side, Galoc, Maglalambay and Panlaitan stay under 7.5 kt, and Tara, Decabobo and Turda under 5 kt. Current is the second factor at the Tara and Turda pickups and overnight in the west. Rain is light: showers about 9 AM–2 PM in the west (up to 0.9 mm/h), drizzle on the Coron side about noon–5 PM and midnight–3 AM. 24h totals are 2.1–7.2 mm (most at Linapacan and Barangonan).

pagasa.detail: PAGASA: no gale, wind signal or heavy-rain warning for Calamian / MIMAROPA. The feed still references the Tropical Cyclone Alert for Typhoon Rosal (Champi) , not covering Palawan. The latest items (to Mon 26 Oct 5:26 AM PHT) are final general flood advisories for the Visayas regions, none covering Palawan.

changed.title: ⚠️ What changed since yesterday afternoon
items: Thursday's west-side wind came in lighter than forecast. Nangalao, Cabunlawan, Decabaitot, Ciron and Barangonan are at 10–16 kt now (gusts to 21), not the 16–20 kt with gusts to 25 expected yesterday. Cabunlawan, Decabaitot and Barangonan also ease to about 9–10 kt around 1–4 PM, and the regional Thursday forecast dropped to 7.4 kt, gusts 13 (was 14 kt, gusts 20). Morning showers are lighter too (4–7 mm in the west, was 7–8.5).

So Friday 30 arrivals improve to SLIGHTLY SOFT (was SOFT). Today stays SOFT because it lands yesterday's windy-day catch. The grounds now read 8 GOOD / 7 MARGINAL / 1 POOR / 0 VERY POOR (was 5 / 5 / 6 / 0 at 2 PM). Saturday turns breezier (9.8 kt, gusts 16, was 5.3 kt) with 9.2 mm of rain, and Friday is no longer dry (3.5 mm). PAGASA has nothing for Palawan.

supply.label: Today Thu
supply.note: Lands yesterday's catch, when the west and Linapacan were blown out at 16–20 kt; mostly Coron-side and southern fish

supply.label: 24h Fri 30
supply.note: Today's lighter wind lets the Coron side and the south fish fully and the west work the 1–4 PM lull; Nangalao and Ciron still contribute little

supply.label: 48h Sat 31
supply.note: Friday is calm (7.0 kt) with only light showers, so most of the fleet goes out and lands Saturday

supply.label: 3d Sun 1
supply.note: Saturday is breezier and wetter (9.8 kt, gusts 16, 9.2 mm), trimming small-boat trips

supply.label: 5–7d
supply.note: Sun 1 and Mon 2 are breezy (10–11 kt, gusts 16–17), trimming Monday and Tuesday arrivals; Tue 3 is the best day, so Wed 4 arrivals firm up. Medium confidence this far out

shortageRisk: Surge flag OFF (unchanged). Shortage risk stays ELEVATED on the dashboard's detector for Thu–Mon (guide only). Today is the tightest day for arrivals; Friday is now only slightly soft. Lean on the Coron side, Panlaitan, Maglalambay, Galoc, Decabobo, Tara and Turda for today's and tomorrow's landings.

bestWindow.headline: Now to about noon on the Coron side and sheltered grounds; 1–4 PM lull in the west
details: 6 AM–noon: Coron, Galoc, Maglalambay, Decabobo and Panlaitan 0.0–0.5 kt, wind under 6 kt, dry. Panlaitan stays easy all day. The dashboard's lowest combined score is Decabobo about 2 PM.
1–4 PM: Cabunlawan, Decabaitot and Barangonan 0.3–0.6 kt with wind down to 9–10 kt, after the showers clear.

Keep small boats off Nangalao and Ciron all day (13–18 kt, gusts to 21), off Cabunlawan, Decabaitot and Barangonan before about 11 AM and after 7 PM, off Tara and Turda during the 7–10 PM pickup, and off Decabaitot, Barangonan and Alava about 1–5 AM Fri (1.2–1.5 kt).
